name: AZ-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Paul Gosar running for reelection with a large cash advantage
No public general-election polling; prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
Challenger fundraising modest with little cash on hand
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Gosar: a deep Republican lean, incumbency, and a fundraising edge over a challenger who has raised little and holds minimal cash. Markets price Democratic odds around 3%, consistent with a Likely Republican rating rather than Safe given the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or a major scandal or outside spending surge against Gosar, would warrant moving this race toward Tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Paul Gosar seeks another term in a northern Arizona district that leans heavily Republican, giving him a structural advantage of roughly fifteen points. He enters the general election with a substantial cash-on-hand lead over Dani Sterbinsky, who has raised a modest sum and spent most of what she collected.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a three percent chance of winning. The forecast therefore rests on district fundamentals, which favor the incumbent by a wide but not insurmountable margin. Gosar is a heavy favorite, though the lack of polling keeps some uncertainty in the estimate.
